audit.whatIsWrong: Full chart gave Ryze first item and 2+ items (and Skill on 4-5/6) while content win[] and the packet chart give Talon all seven rows.
audit.why: 56.43% WR over 863 games plus both data sources agree Talon holds every stage; Ryze's spike is three-plus items, past this chart's horizon per the content text itself.
audit.corrected: Full rows 3-6 aligned to Talon with rewritten whys.

audit.why: Spikes at 1-3, 6, first item, late-deny are present and coherent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Talon's R called 'Shadow Assassin' in spikes[1] and whys[4]; content twice describes Rune Prison as self-castable ('self-root shield', 'blowing W on himself') — Ryze's W cages an enemy target, not himself; cooldowns field had no digits and packet flags zero sequencing advice.
audit.why: Kit: Rune Prison 11s targeted cage (roots only with Flux), E Spell Flux 3.5s, Q Overload 5s, R Realm Warp 180s. Riot's W text has no self-cast.
audit.corrected: Names fixed, self-cast W claims replaced, real cooldowns and sequencing added.

edits.before: - Ryze Rune Prison (Root): matchup-defining — Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E Assassin's Path for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Ryze Rune Prison (Root): 11s at rank 1 — it only roots with Flux on you; step up in its downtime. - His E is 3.5s and Q 5s, so the spam never stops — commit fast, never slow-walk in. - Budget your E for emergencies, the R for opportunities.

edits.before: W on the contact, Q the gap, auto for the bleed, walk through the return — three stacks of rent he paid for one trade.
edits.after: Every last-hit step-up is a W-slow into Q blink — the bleed stacks up before his 11-second Rune Prison can answer.

edits.before: Q-leaping into a held CC for style — Talon without the gap-closer is a roamer stuck in traffic.
edits.after: An uncrashed wave is free scaling gold for Ryze — crash it so the roam costs him plates and pings.

edits.before: Ryze is one of the weakest early laners in the game, low base damage, clunky Q-E combo, and no mobility until his E-flux resets are online. With W (Rake) plus Q (Noxian Diplomacy) you stack bleed and blink on him the second he steps up to last-hit, and his only defense is Flash or a poorly-timed W (Rune Prison) self-root shield.
edits.after: Ryze is one of the weakest early laners in the game, low base damage, clunky Q-E combo, and no mobility until his E-flux resets are online. With W (Rake) plus Q (Noxian Diplomacy) you stack bleed and blink on him the second he steps up to last-hit, and his only defense is Flash or catching you with a W (Rune Prison) cage.

edits.before: Shadow Assassin (R) turns his lane into a nightmare: he has no escape from the stealth engage and no burst to answer yours. Use R to all-in him outright or to roam, since Ryze contributes almost nothing to the map before he has three items and Ryze cannot punish your absence.
edits.after: Shadow Assault (R) turns his lane into a nightmare: he has no escape from the stealth engage and no burst to answer yours. Use R to all-in him outright or to roam, since Ryze contributes almost nothing to the map before he has three items and Ryze cannot punish your absence.

edits.before: At level 6 Shadow Assassin gives you an unanswerable engage against a champ with no escape.
edits.after: At level 6 Shadow Assault gives you an unanswerable engage against a champ with no escape.

edits.before: Ryze is helpless at levels 1-3: his damage is low, his combo is mana-hungry and slow, and he has zero mobility to escape your gap-close. Take W first to poke and shove, then punish every last-hit step with a W-slow into Q blink that stacks passive bleed. His only outs are Flash or blowing W (Rune Prison) on himself, both of which you can bait and re-engage on.
edits.after: Ryze is helpless at levels 1-3: his damage is low, his combo is mana-hungry and slow, and he has zero mobility to escape your gap-close. Take W first to poke and shove, then punish every last-hit step with a W-slow into Q blink that stacks passive bleed. His only outs are Flash or catching you with W (Rune Prison), both of which you can bait and re-engage on.

edits.before: Bleed-string the contacts: W both passes, Q the gap, auto the third stack. The lane bleeds rent.
edits.after: Through 4-5 you all-in freely — Ryze cannot trade back fast enough or punish a single roam.

edits.before: Shadow Assault online — the roam game doubles and the all-in wraps targets in a blade carousel.
edits.after: Shadow Assault online — an unanswerable stealth engage on a champ with no escape but Flash.

edits.before: First item spike: the full string one-rotations squishies. Shove and parkour — side lanes owe you taxes.
edits.after: First item: Dirk-Hydra deletes him well before the mana-scaling burst arrives — dive with E resets.

edits.before: Late Talon flanks from coordinates wards don't cover: R in, string the carry, blade-exit through the wall.
edits.after: Into two items you still out-burst and out-roam him — hunt the pick before Realm Warp fights form.

notes: No report edits needed (no lint findings there). Full rows 3-6 disagreed with content win[] and packet (all Talon); aligned. 'Point-blank root' phrasing in dosFull[0].d/report[5].t is loose (W is a 615-range targeted cage that only roots with Flux) but not flagged and defensible as shorthand — left alone to conserve the report cap; noted for the user. Content's 'self-root shield' claim about Rune Prison was removed as unsupported by Riot's text.
